Chief Executive’s Foreword 
 
I hope you all had a very pleasant Easter. Spring is a time 
of regeneration and growth and last month Fingal County 
Council continued to promote our county wide tree 
planting programme by giving away 8,000 native and non-
native tree species to residents for planting in their own 
gardens during National Tree Week. The health, social and 
ecological benefit of trees is well documented and since 
2019, Fingal County Council has given away over 60,000 
trees reflecting our commitment to boosting tree cover and 
enhancing species diversity. This year marks the 40th 
anniversary of the founding of the Tree Council of Ireland 
and we were very pleased to welcome President of Ireland 
Catherine Connolly to Newbridge House and Demesne on 
March 8th to officially launch the National Tree Week 
programme. President Connolly also took part in a tree 
planting ceremony in the grounds and learned about the 
tree species and history of this magnificent heritage site. 
Newbridge Demesne forms part of our 2,300 hectares of 
public open space and is an excellent example of a space 
which is defined by its woodlands and majestic, mature 
trees which provide such enjoyment for visitors. I wish to 
thank our Parks & Green Infrastructure Division and our 
Operations teams who facilitated this year’s tree giveaway 
at 7 locations across Fingal and I hope all the recipients 
reap the rewards which come with tending these trees. 
 
Last month significant milestones were marked in the 
progression of the R132 Connectivity Project in Swords 
with the appointment of Murphy as the contractor and the 
subsequent signing of the multi-million euro contract in 
County Hall. The project, which is being funded by the NTA, 
will take 25 months to complete and will be carried out in 
four phases along the 3km route from the Bostik junction 
to the edge of the Pinnock Hill roundabout. The first phase 
of the works will see the Estuary Roundabout being 
replaced by a 4-point junction which will be safer and more 
accessible for road users and pedestrians. The project 
objective is to enhance functionality of the R132 while 
supporting 
the 
development 
of 
BusConnects 
and 
MetroLink which will deliver more sustainable, accessible 
transport links for the people of the county. The contractor, 
Murphy, has a stellar reputation as a transportation 
specialist and has previously delivered sustainable 
infrastructure solutions on an international scale as well as 
high profile projects here at home. Cognisant of the 
projection that the population of Swords is set to double 
over the next 20 years, the R132 Connectivity Project will 
provide safe and efficient connectivity within the town and 
its transformation will  
 
 
support sustainable growth as part of the Sustainable 
Swords Strategy. A sod turning on the R132 on Friday, 
March 27th signified the beginning of the works and was 
attended by Minister for Transport, Darragh O’Brien TD 
along with The Mayor of Fingal and Elected Members, 
representatives of MetroLink, TII and NTA and community 
stakeholders. Meticulous traffic management planning has 
taken place to ensure that the R132, which is a major 
commuter corridor, will remain open for the duration of 
the works. Two lanes in each direction — northbound and 
southbound — will remain open during peak traffic hours 
(6:30am - 10:00am and 4:00pm - 7:30pm)  to ensure traffic 
at peak commuter times is minimally affected. Traffic 
impact will be continuously monitored and managed 
throughout the project.  I look forward to bringing you 
updates on the progress of this project in the coming 
months.  
 
The Community Development and Inclusion Office recently 
marked the 19th year of World Autism Awareness Day by 
compiling sensory kits which were distributed to ten 
community centres across Fingal. The sensory kits contain 
items designed to support regulation, comfort, and 
wellbeing for children and adults with sensory processing 
needs. This initiative aligns with training provided by AsIAm 
to the Fingal Community Facilities network in June 2025 
and highlights our ongoing commitment to fostering 
inclusivity, accessibility and respect in our communities 
and shared spaces. The 2026 observance of World Autism 
Awareness Day (WAAD), themed “Autism and Humanity – 
Every Life Has Value,” highlights and affirms the dignity and 
worth of all autistic people. I wish to commend the staff  for 
their tireless work in promoting initiatives which seek to 
include those who face barriers and challenges in their 
everyday lives.  
 
Finally, I wish to formally welcome Sinéad Murphy as she 
attends her first Council Meeting as Director of Service for 
Operations. 
Sinéad 
was 
appointed 
following 
the 
retirement of Mary T. Daly in March and brings to the role 
a wealth of knowledge and experience amassed in her 
previous appointments including in Water Services, 
Transportation and Planning & Strategic Infrastructure. 
Most recently, Sinéad was the Senior Engineer with the 
Active Travel Unit and worked on many high-profile 
projects within the county. I know you will join me in 
wishing Sinéad all the very best as she embarks on this new 
chapter in her career.    
 
Best wishes, 
AnnMarie Farrelly 
Chief Executive

St. Patricks Day Celebrations in New York 
A Fingal County Council delegation visited New York 
from Sunday March 15th to Wednesday March 18th 
to promote the new Fingal Tourism Destination 
Brand Explore Fingal and develop opportunities for 
economic development and tourism promotion with 
local elected officials, media, tourism, cultural and 
business representatives. The Mayor had the honour 
of raising the Irish flag at the Irish/US flag raising 
ceremony marking the start of St Patrick’s day 
celebrations in New York City.

The delegation supported the launch of the American 
250 programme and the expansion of the Global 
Irish Famine Way (National Famine Way) into the US. 
Additional meetings were also held to strengthen the 
Council’s links with the IDA, Tourism Ireland, the 
Dublin Society and Irish American / NY business, 
tourism and cultural associations.

Youth & Education 
 
 
Fingal County Council Arts Office and Superprojects 
are finalising a very special arts-in education project 
publication titled Seanchaí Microforest (2020–24).

Seanchaí Microforest was conceived by artist Gareth 
Kennedy during the pandemic of 2020 as a means to 
work with artists and young people outdoors. It is 
now a thriving habitat that serves as an outdoor 
learning and recreation space, addressing climate 
action at a local level, while also enhancing students' 
mental and physical wellbeing. This publication 
offers insight into the origins of the Microforest 
method and its compelling value in our lives. It 
reveals the unique seasonal and creative workshops 
supported by artists and ecological experts over a 4-
year period on site. It is hoped that this project will 
inspire further radical acts of afforestation in other 
educational settings and beyond. A publication 
launch event will be announced shortly.

Preventing Homelessness, Notices to Quit and 
Tenant In-situ Acquisitions  
Fingal County Council is aware that households in the 
Fingal area who may have received a notice to quit, 
which is also referred to as a notice of termination, 
from their landlord may be worried or unsure of 
what to do.  Fingal County Council and the Dublin 
Regional Homeless Executive (DRHE) would like to 
advise anyone affected of the services that are 
available to them in these circumstances.  
 
We strongly encourage tenants residing in the 
Fingal area, who have been issued with a notice 
of termination, to contact Fingal County Council 
as soon as they receive a notice from their 
landlord. The contact details for Fingal County 
Council are provided at the bottom of this page.  
When the tenants contact Fingal County Council, staff in 
the Housing Department will take note of the termination 
date.  
 
The Council advises the tenant to refer the notice to 
Threshold, a service funded by the DRHE to provide a 
Tenancy Protection Service for private renters in the Dublin 
Region, including Fingal. Threshold can also be contacted 
directly on Freephone 1800 454 454 or via their website 
www.threshold.ie which contains more information and 
advice on the validity of your notice.  
 
The Council’s first response will be to try to prevent 
homelessness. This includes assessing the person’s 
position on the social housing list, providing advice on 
applying for Choice Based Lettings, and advising the 
person on the level of Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) 
they may be eligible to receive. 
  
Placement in emergency accommodation will be a last 
resort if no other alternative can be identified.

Fingal County Council continues to liaise with other 
Dublin and neighboring local authorities to deal with 
tenancy issues that may require an inter-authority 
approach.  In particular, we are working closely with 
our colleagues in the other Dublin Local Authorities 
on the implementation of the Government policy and 
guidance, with a focus on the needs of tenants.   
  
Whilst the Council will, in the context of current 
circumstances, adopt flexibility in dealing with 
potential acquisitions of properties with tenants in 
situ, any acquisition is subject to appropriate due 
diligence and checks before any commitment is 
made to acquire, including, for example, determining 
that a valid notice of termination is in place, the 
tenant has a social housing need, and the condition 
and valuation of the property.  
  
The Government has put forward options to allow 
tenants who are not eligible for social housing to 
remain in their homes, including schemes to support 
the purchase of homes and a Cost Rental in-situ 
Scheme. The Cost Rental Tenant-in-Situ Scheme is 
available for tenants who are not eligible for social 
housing and are at risk of homelessness.  
 
The DHLGH has advised that local authorities are to 
be the first point of contact for this scheme, but it is 
managed by the Housing Agency. Under the scheme, 
the Housing Agency can purchase a property and 
rent it to the tenant. Fingal County Council will 
undertake an initial assessment of the tenant’s 
circumstances and refer details to the Housing 
Agency for consideration, where the tenant is at risk 
of homelessness and the Cost Rental Tenant-in-Situ 
scheme applies. The Housing Agency will then 
contact the landlord about the purchase of the 
property.  
  
Where a tenant wishes to purchase their home from 
the landlord, local authorities can provide advice 
about the Local Authority Home Loan scheme. The 
Government is examining implementing a ‘right of 
first refusal’ for tenants to purchase their homes, as 
well as expanding the First Home shared equity 
scheme. The Council will be able to provide more 
information on these when available.

Developer Lead Infrastructure Initiative (DLI) for

The Government’s Housing Action Plan, ‘Delivering 
Homes, Building Communities’ seeks to deliver 
300,000 new homes by 2030. It identifies the need for 
the provision of enabling infrastructure, including 
wastewater infrastructure, to support the delivery of 
new 
residential 
development, 
particularly 
in 
locations where wastewater infrastructure capacity is 
constrained or absent. This objective is set out in 
Action 1.11 of the Housing Action Plan and is further 
referenced in Action 15(ii) of the ‘Accelerating 
Infrastructure Taskforce Report & Plan’. 
 
Wastewater infrastructural constraints have been 
identified as a limiting factor for housing delivery in 
settlements where existing Uisce Éireann wastewater 
treatment capacity is not immediately available. 
 
To address this, the Government is now enabling 
housing developers to deliver new wastewater 
infrastructure as part of their housing schemes. The 
Developer-Led Infrastructure (DLI) Initiative for 
wastewater services includes the following key 
coordinated elements: 
 
• a structured partnership approach between Uisce 
Éireann and developers,enabling developers to 
construct wastewater infrastructure to Uisce 
Éireann standards, with transfer of ownership to 
Uisce Éireann for longterm operation and 
maintenance; 
• regulatory reform to simplify environmental 
authorisations for discharges from small-scale 
treatment facilities; an 
• specific guidance for developers from Uisce 
Éireann and the Environmental Protection Agency 
(EPA) in relation to standards and requirements. 
 
This Circular is accompanied by a Procedural Advice 
Note to set out the procedural arrangements 
associated with the DLI Initiative in the context of 
planning applications lodged by developers for such 
infrastructure as part of proposals for new housing 
development.
